question: Chetan travels from City A to City B. If Chetan drives his car at (3)/(4) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 33 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Chetan would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (Normal : New) = 4 : 3

Since distance is constant, Time ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 4

Difference in time ratio parts = 4 − 3 = 1 part.

Given 1 part = 33 minutes.

Normal time (3 parts) = 33 × 3 = 99 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 99 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 
 
 City A
 City B

 
 Speed = S, Time = T
 
 
 Speed = 3/4 S, Time = T + 33

**Given:**

New Speed = 3/4 of Normal Speed

Delay time = 33 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the normal speed be S and the normal time taken be T.

⇒ Distance D = S × T

In the second case, New Speed = 3S/4

⇒ New Time taken = Distance ÷ New Speed

⇒ New Time = D ÷ (3S/4) = 4D / 3S

Substitute D = S × T into the new time equation:

⇒ New Time = 4 × (S × T) / 3S = 4T/3

The difference between the new time and normal time is given as 33 minutes.

⇒ (4T/3) − T = 33

⇒ (4T − 3T) / 3 = 33

⇒ T/3 = 33

⇒ T = 33 × 3 = 99 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 99 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance covered is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional to each other. S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

Average Speed is the ratio of Total Distance to Total Time. If equal distance is covered at speeds A and B, then Average Speed = (2 × A × B) / (A + B).

Relative Speed

For two bodies moving in opposite directions, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (|S₁ − S₂|).
